scenes.label: Meet Meera
scenes.title: A happy mix
scenes.caption: Meera's evening routine: homework, then twenty minutes of videos. Her feed is usually a happy mix. Science experiments from his favourite channel, How It Works. Cricket highlights. A cooking video her dad sent her. Some music. She likes that it always seems to know what she enjoys, and she never really wonders how.

scenes.label: The rabbit hole
scenes.title: Scarier and angrier
scenes.caption: But after the fake fair clip, her feed changes. She replayed that clip again and again while checking it for clues. Now there are more fair cancelled videos, then scarier ones: shocking truth, you won't believe this. Angry faces, red arrows. Her science videos have vanished. Meera keeps scrolling, and she feels more and more anxious.
scenes.dialogue: Why is my whole feed about this now?

scenes.label: How feeds learn
scenes.title: Every tap is a signal.
scenes.caption: Meera looks up how feeds work. The app records every signal: clicks, replays, pauses, how long you watch. A recommendation algorithm uses those signals to predict what will keep you watching. This is called engagement. Shocking, angry videos grab attention, so they get pushed further. Less and less variety gets through. That's a filter bubble.
scenes.dialogue: My fact-checking replays taught it I loved rumours!

scenes.label: Steer the feed
scenes.title: Send better signals.
scenes.caption: Your turn. Help Meera steer her feed back to variety. Use Not interested on the rumour videos, search for topics she actually enjoys, and follow a reliable news source. Watch the topic variety meter. Careful: tapping one more shocking video, even just to check it, teaches the algorithm to send even more.
scenes.dialogue: Every tap is a signal. Let's send better ones.

scenes.label: Back in control
scenes.title: Attention isn't truth.
scenes.caption: The meter climbs back up. Science, cricket, music, and real news from the fair's official page. The algorithm isn't evil, and it can't read minds. It just follows your signals and rewards attention, not truth. So Meera steers on purpose: she turns off autoplay, and when a feed makes her anxious, she takes a break and talks to someone.
scenes.dialogue: It rewards attention, not truth. I steer it.

scenes.label: A happier ending
scenes.title: His feed, his choices
scenes.caption: A week later, Meera's feed feels like hers again. She even films a short video about her water tester for her favourite channel's viewer challenge. At dinner, she shows her parents how to reset a feed, and her dad laughs: so that's why I only see cricket! Your turn: help Meera spot how feeds shift, one click at a time.
scenes.dialogue: My feed, my choices, one signal at a time.
